text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
U.S. Polar explorer ROBERT PEARY was born in 1856.

Austrian psychiatrist and pioneer of pyschoanalysis SIGMUND FREUD was born in 1856. He was the first to put forward the theory that experiences in early childhood, could lead to problems in later life.
Perth Town Clerk WILLIAM BOLD was born in 1873. He was a pioneer of town planning.
Screen legend RUDOLPH VALENTINO was born in 1895. the Italian actor became a Hollywood heart throb from performances in films such as "The Sheik".
The founder of the Australian Surf Lifesaving Movement, WALTER BIDDELL, was born in 1907. He first started surf lifesaving at Bronte beach in 1907.

Film-maker, actor, and radio pioneer ORSON WELLES was born in 1915. WELLES' first film "Citizen Kane" is considered by many to be the greatest movie ever made. He's best remembered for his powerful voice, and for a radio performance of the H.G. WELLS's "War of the Worlds", which was so realistic, it caused thousands of Americans to take to the streets in panic.

US singer/songwriter BOB SEGER was born in 1945. He released his first album in his own name in 1966, after performing with a series of bands. Hits included "Ramblin' Gamblin' Man" (1968), "Night Moves" (1976), "Still The Same" (1978), "Fire Lake"
(1980), "Against The Wind" (1980), "Shame On The Moon" (1982) and "Shake Down" (1987).
** EVENTS **
1626 : A Dutch settler, PETER MINUIT, bought what is now
Manhattan Island from the Indians for a handful of trinkets worth no more than 25 dollars.
1733 : The first international boxing match was held in
London. It was won by Englishman BOB WHITTAKER, who beat Italy's TITO DE CARNI.
1839 : The founder of Melbourne, JOHN BATMAN died at the
age of 38.
1840 : The first adhesive postage stamps, the Penny Black
and the Twopenny Blue, went on sale in Britain.
1851 : American inventor LINUS YALE patented the padlock.
1861 : Arkansas voted to secede from the Union and join
the Confederacy.
1882 : British statesman Lord CAVENDISH was murdered by
Irish nationalists soon after arriving in Dublin as chief secretary to the Lord Lieutenant of Ireland.
1910 : EDWARD VII, king of Great Britain and Ireland and
Emperor of India from January 1901, died. His son acceeded to the throne as GEORGE V.
1919 : The Paris Peace Conference disposed of Germany's

colonies; German East Africa was assigned as a League of Nations mandate to Britain and France, German South-West Africa as a mandate to South Africa. German New Guinea was assigned as a League of Nations mandate to Australia.
1937 : The airship Hindenburg exploded while docking at
Lakehurst,New Jersey. 36 people were killed. The accident ended the era of hydrogen-based airships.
1942 : US Forces on the Philippine island of Corregidor
surrendered to the Japanese. The prisoners later took part in what became known as the Bataan Death march.
1954 : British athlete ROGER BANNISTER became the first
athlete to run a mile in under four minutes, recording a time of 3 minutes 59.4 seconds.
1976 : An earthquake in Northern Italy killed 900 people.
1980 : JOHN CAIN unsuccessfully challenged FRANK WILKES
for the leadership of the Victorian Labor Party. He lost 16 to 29. In September 1981 CAIN finally became leader of the Labor Opposition.
1992 : MARLENE DIETRICH, film's legendary femme

fatale, died. The German-born actress shot to fame as cabaret singer Lola-Lola in "The Blue Angel" and then took Hollywood by storm with such classics as "The Scarlet Empress", "Dishonoured" and "The Devil is a Woman".
1994 : NELSON MANDELA and his ANC, finally confirmed as
runaway victors of South Africa's historic elections, named their team for a post-apartheid government of national unity.
1994 : Historic rivals Britain and France were joined for
the first time since the Ice Age by an undersea tunnel hailed as one of the great engineering feats of the 20th century.
1996 : The body of former CIA Director WILLIAM COLBY was
found at a river's edge nine days after he apparently drowned while canoeing near his weekend home in southern Maryland.
